Fix an optimizer at (K,x), match a point of K' to K within Hausdorff distance, and move the mark from x to x'. The denominator can drop by at most η/r, where η=d_H(K,K')+||x−x'||. The same estimate works for either body and either mark with that optimizer, and the denominator is affine along interpolated marks. The own-body bound 1/(d+1) therefore gives a common floor of 1/[2(d+1)] for both optimizers in both tests after shrinking the product neighborhood.

Translate by the common inball center y. The inclusion δB_d⊂(δ/R)(K−y) and the convex identity for the sum of two positive dilations of K−y give the claimed dilation bound. Thus |K'∖K| is at most [(1+δ/R)^d−1]|K|, and the reverse difference uses |K'|. On a bounded δ interval this is uniformly O(δ).

The mark derivative of the tested integrand has norm at most (d+1)r^(−1)[2(d+1)]^(d+2), and the integrand itself is uniformly bounded by [2(d+1)]^(d+1). Integrating the mark difference on K∩K' and using the symmetric-difference bound, the two optimality tests give a uniform bound on the absolute energy difference. Every denominator has mean one over its centered marked ball. Jensen gives a uniform lower bound |rB_d| for both optimal energies, allowing the d-th root and the Hausdorff estimate to produce the claimed relative local Lipschitz bound.

Both signs of each continuous displacement remain in the own-fiber interior, so one-sided slope inequalities force the continuous component of every supergradient to equal the envelope derivative. Dividing the base component by positive F_0 gives B in span(Q−Q). The chart equals 1/(d+1) plus d/(d+1) times the bracket, and positive F forces a positive bracket at every interior mark. Density of interior points within each real fiber yields the weak floor on all C.

The radius 1+sqrt(z) is positive, concave and continuous on [0,1], so the ambient set is compact convex with full-dimensional ball fibers. Every admissible denominator at the ball center has mean one. Jensen gives energy at least the volume, attained by a=0. The energy-root secant quotient from (0,0) along (z,0) equals |B_d|^(1/d)/sqrt(z), which diverges.
